taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; Uber operates only in a limited way, so booking a taxi by phone or app or using a rank is often easier.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-wide emergency number; 15 reaches the SAMU medical service, 17 the police, and 18 the fire brigade.

hood_landmark.Vieille Ville (Old Town): Cours Lafayette market old town Toulon

avoid.reason: Peripheral housing estates like La Beaucaire and Sainte-Musse hold nothing for visitors and are best skipped.
Parts of the old lower town's narrow lanes feel seedy late at night; watch for pickpockets around the port and the Cours Lafayette market.

hood_desc: Toulon's dense Provençal old town of narrow lanes, painted facades, and fountains, centred on the daily Cours Lafayette market; the atmospheric first-timer base packed with sights, cafes, and character.
A charming seaside village district east of the centre with sandy beaches, a small fishing port, palm-lined promenades, and family restaurants; relaxed, residential, and popular for a calmer stay.
The lively harbour front along Quai Cronstadt, where ferries and navy ships share the Rade, backed by a strip of bars, brasseries, and boat departures for the Îles d'Hyères; a central, animated base.

The 19th-century upper town of wide avenues around Place de la Liberté and the Opera, with department stores, boulevards, and grand facades; a walkable, well-connected central district for shopping and dining.
A working-class residential neighbourhood west of the centre with a local market, everyday shops, and affordable lodging; light on sights but handy and inexpensive for budget travellers.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France.

transit.hours: Réseau Mistral (RMTT) buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 8:30 PM with some evening lines; the 'bateaux-bus' harbour shuttles run through the day.
transit.note: Toulon has no metro or tram; the Réseau Mistral (RMTT) runs the city buses plus 'bateaux-bus' boat-buses across the Rade harbour to La Seyne, Les Sablettes and Saint-Mandrier, and seasonal ferries to the Îles d'Hyères.
transit.pay: Buy a single ticket from the driver or machines (~€1.40) or a rechargeable Mistral pass; the same ticket covers the bateaux-bus harbour shuttles.

ferry: Seasonal ferries to the Îles d'Hyères (Porquerolles)

transit.m: Réseau Mistral line 102/191 bus to Toulon center (~35-45 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law ('service compris'); rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated but not required.

food.name: Cade toulonnaise
food.desc: Toulon's chickpea-flour pancake, baked in a wood oven until thicker and more charred than Nice's socca, eaten hot in paper with black pepper.

places.name: La Cade a Dede
places.note: Wood-fired cade specialist by the daily market; the local reference for the dish.

places.name: Marche du Cours Lafayette
places.note: Morning market where cade sellers work the crowds; buy a wedge and eat standing up.

places.name: Les Halles de Toulon
places.note: Covered food hall with Provencal stalls, an easy indoor place to find cade and panisses.

food.name: Chichi fregi
food.desc: Long ridged Provencal doughnut fried to order, rolled in sugar and scented with orange-flower water. A Toulon beach and fairground fixture.

places.name: Chichi Fregi
places.note: Dedicated chichi shop in a Provencal-themed room, praised for warm welcome and fresh frying.

places.name: Plages du Mourillon stands
places.note: Beachfront kiosks fry chichis through summer; the traditional way to eat them.

places.name: Marche du Cours Lafayette
places.note: Market vendors fry chichis alongside the cade on busy mornings.

food.name: Bouillabaisse
food.desc: Mediterranean rock-fish stew served in two parts: saffron broth with rouille and croutons first, then the fish carved at the table.

places.name: Au Sourd
places.note: Toulon's most historic seafood restaurant, trading since the 1860s; a classic bouillabaisse.

places.name: Le Gros Ventre
places.note: Seafront address long known for bouillabaisse and whole grilled fish.

places.name: Le Neptunia
places.note: Terrace restaurant doing refined seasonal Provencal cooking with a strong fish list.

food.name: Soupe au pistou
food.desc: Late-summer Provencal vegetable and bean soup finished with a pounded basil, garlic and olive oil pistou stirred in at the table.

places.name: Au Sourd
places.note: Old-guard kitchen that keeps Provencal staples like pistou soup on the menu.

places.name: Les Halles de Toulon
places.note: Food-hall traiteurs sell pistou soup in season, plus the basil and beans to make it.

places.name: Le Neptunia
places.note: Seasonal menu that leans on Provencal vegetables when summer produce peaks.

food.name: Panisses
food.desc: Chickpea-flour batons set firm, then deep fried until crisp outside and creamy inside. Salted, squeezed with lemon, eaten with a drink.

places.name: La Cade a Dede
places.note: Fries panisses next to the cade; the pair is the local snack order.

places.name: Marche du Cours Lafayette
places.note: Several stalls sell panisses raw to fry at home or already fried to eat there.

places.name: Plages du Mourillon stands
places.note: Beach kiosks and casual bars serve panisses as a seaside aperitif snack.

food.name: Grilled fish from the Toulon boats
food.desc: Sardines, daurade, rouget and loup grilled whole with olive oil and fennel, landed on the quay at the Port and sold the same morning.

places.name: Au Sourd
places.note: Whole fish from the day's catch, filleted at the table; a Toulon rite of passage.

places.name: Le Gros Ventre
places.note: Seaside terrace specialising in simply grilled Mediterranean fish and shellfish.

places.name: Quai de la Sinse fish stalls
places.note: Harbour fish sellers where restaurants buy; good for seeing what is in season.

food.name: Pastis
food.desc: Anise aperitif diluted with iced water until cloudy, the ritual drink of Provence and the standard order on any Toulon terrace before lunch.

places.name: Port de Toulon quayside bars
places.note: Row of harbour terraces where locals take a pastis before eating; ferry-watching included.

places.name: Place Puget cafes
places.note: Shaded square around the mossy fountain, the classic old-town aperitif spot.

places.name: Plages du Mourillon stands
places.note: Beach bars pour pastis with panisses in the late afternoon.

food.name: Bandol and Coteaux Varois wine
food.desc: Toulon sits between two appellations: mourvedre-heavy Bandol reds and rose just west, and fresher Coteaux Varois wines from the hills inland.

places.name: Le Neptunia
places.note: Local-leaning wine list with Bandol and Var bottles to match the seafood.

places.name: Au Sourd
places.note: Long-established cellar strong on Provencal rose to drink with bouillabaisse.

places.name: Les Halles de Toulon
places.note: Wine counters in the covered market pour local appellations by the glass.

landmarks: Mont Faron and Téléphérique
France's only Mediterranean cable car climbs 584 metres to pine-clad Mont Faron, unveiling one of Europe's most spectacular harbour panoramas over Toulon's roadstead.
Rade de Toulon (Harbour Boat Tour)
Cruise Europe's finest natural anchorage, home port of France's navy, gliding past aircraft carriers, forts and the glittering bays of Saint-Mandrier and La Seyne.
Musée National de la Marine
Beside the monumental Puget-carved gateway of the old arsenal, this naval museum displays grand ship models, figureheads and centuries of Toulon's maritime glory.
Cours Lafayette Market
Provence comes alive each morning along this plane-shaded avenue, where stalls heap olives, herbs and sun-ripened produce amid the cries of Provençal vendors.
Toulon Cathedral (Sainte-Marie-de-la-Seds)
Hidden in the old town's lanes, the 11th-century cathedral blends Romanesque bones with a Baroque facade and a bell tower crowned by wrought iron.
Mémorial du Débarquement de Provence
Atop Mont Faron, this memorial museum in the Beaumont Tower honours the August 1944 Allied landings that liberated southern France, with moving multimedia exhibits.
Tour Royale
A squat 16th-century royal cannon tower guarding the harbour mouth now hosts exhibitions, picnickers and swimmers on the rocky point of Le Mourillon.
Plages du Mourillon
Toulon's family-friendly crescent of landscaped beaches and gardens curves toward Fort Saint-Louis, lined with restaurants and views across the shimmering bay.
Opéra de Toulon
France's second-largest opera house, an opulent 1862 jewel of gilt and velvet, anchors the elegant squares and fountains of Toulon's Haussmannian quarter.
Place Puget and the Old Town Fountains
The mossy Fontaine des Trois Dauphins, sprouting greenery since 1780, epitomises the shabby-chic charm of old Toulon's fountain-studded pedestrian lanes.

train.note: Toulon is on the Mediterranean main line, with TGV services to Paris in about 4 hours and Marseille in 45 minutes, and TER trains east along the coast to Saint-Raphaël, Cannes and Nice. Through services toward Ventimiglia and Italy run from Nice, so most Italy journeys involve a change. The station is central. SNCF advance fares open around six months ahead.

bus.note: Coaches use the terminal beside the railway station. FlixBus and BlaBlaCar Bus run along the coast to Nice, Marseille and into Italy and Spain. Zou! regional buses serve the Var coast and Hyères. Carry your passport or EU ID card for cross-border services.

intl.to: Bastia, Ajaccio, Île-Rousse & Propriano, Corsica (France) - ~6-10 hr
Porquerolles, Port-Cros & Le Levant (France) - Îles d'Hyères

ferry.note: Toulon is one of the main French mainland ports for Corsica, with Corsica Ferries sailing year-round and much more frequently in summer - overnight crossings carry cabins and cars. The ferry terminal is on the harbour front in the middle of town. The Îles d'Hyères boats leave from La Tour Fondue on the Giens peninsula, about 30 minutes east, and are the only access to car-free Porquerolles.

half.name: Hyeres
half.blurb: Hyeres is a palm-lined coastal town east of Toulon with a medieval hilltop old quarter and nearby salt marshes.

half.name: Porquerolles
half.blurb: Porquerolles is a car-free island off Hyeres reached by boat, with pine forests, vineyards and clear-water coves.

half.name: Bandol
half.blurb: Bandol is a harbor town west of Toulon known for its rose vineyards and a seafront promenade lined with palms.

half.name: Sanary-sur-Mer
half.blurb: Sanary-sur-Mer is a fishing port west of Toulon with a colorful harbor still used by traditional wooden tuna boats.

half.name: Aix-en-Provence
half.blurb: Aix-en-Provence is a former capital of Provence with fountains, plane-tree boulevards and painter Paul Cezanne's old studio.
